source: CDFI Fund — Certified CDFI List (Native CDFI subset)
publisher: U.S. Treasury, Community Development Financial Institutions Fund
native_identifiability: Authoritative roster of certified Native CDFIs — 69 as of 2025-03-12; Native CDFI = a certified CDFI with >=50% of activities serving Native American, Alaska Native and/or Native Hawaiian people or communities. Downloadable certified-CDFI list (XLSX) flags the Native ones
identity_semantics: COVERAGE FRAME: enumerates the FINANCING INSTITUTIONS serving Indian Country, not Native-owned businesses. A Native CDFI is not necessarily Native-OWNED in the business sense; the >=50%-serving test is an activity test, not an ownership certification. Use it to map the lender layer and as a discovery hub for borrower businesses, never as a business-ownership assertion
export: downloadable certified-CDFI list (XLSX/PDF); CIMS5 mapping via AMIS; Fed Minneapolis 'Mapping Native American Financial Institutions' is a companion map
notes: NEW FRAME: Native CDFIs (the financing<->business layer). Institutions, not businesses -- but the lender map is the hub from which individual borrower businesses are found (rows below). nation_ids: [] (national).

source: Native CDFI Network — member directory & Difference Makers profiles
native_identifiability: Membership directory of Native CDFIs plus 'Difference Makers' profiles; a peer index of the lender universe (complements the CDFI Fund's official list with the member-org view)
identity_semantics: COVERAGE FRAME / org directory: lists Native CDFIs (institutions). Same discipline as the CDFI Fund row — institution membership, not business ownership. Profiles may name individual borrowers (person/business boundary applies to those)
notes: The membership-org counterpart to the CDFI Fund list; useful to cross-check the institution roster and to reach individual CDFIs for borrower-business leads. nation_ids: [] (national).

source: Four Bands Community Fund — client/borrower success stories
publisher: Four Bands Community Fund (Native CDFI, Cheyenne River Sioux Reservation, Eagle Butte SD)
native_identifiability: Prototype of the individual-business discovery path: a Native CDFI's site names client businesses in success stories / incubator spotlights (e.g. Woyute Natural Foods & Apothecary on the Cheyenne River Lakota Reservation); >$53M deployed, 1,300+ jobs
identity_semantics: DISCOVERY ONLY: borrower spotlights are marketing, opt-in, and partial — being a CDFI borrower is not an ownership or citizenship assertion, and these are person/business records (person boundary). Enumerates a handful of named businesses, not a roster
export: web (fourbands.org success-stories / incubator pages) -- narrative, not a list export
notes: One worked example of the borrower-showcase pattern that every Native CDFI on the CDFI Fund list potentially offers -- a repeatable discovery route to individual Native businesses (Chi Ishobak/Pokagon, Lakota Funds, etc. are peers). Discovery grade only. nation_id: bia: Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe.
